## Purpose and safety boundary

This notebook documents the complete subtitle-cleaning design, demonstrates
the deterministic transformations, and audits the current state of the unified
talent DuckDB. It is the working explanation for both the historical backfill
and the future incremental pipeline.

An ordinary render is deliberately **read-only**. With the default parameters,
it does not overwrite raw subtitles, create Parquet files, add DuckDB tables,
or publish sentence rows. Its real subtitle example sends a small cleaned
excerpt to the internal FullStop service so the rendered notebook demonstrates
reconstruction quality. Set `run_punctuation_example:false` for a fully offline
render. Saving the worked example requires the separate
`publish_example:true` parameter.

The core data invariant is:

> `text.subtitle_units` is canonical raw transcript evidence. Cleaned sentences
> are derived data and must preserve lineage back to the contributing
> `subtitle_unit_key` values.

## Current conclusion

The transformation logic, FullStop HTTP client, derived DuckDB schema, and
transactional publisher exist and have been tested. The current batch runner
can still write experimental sentence-level Parquet files, but the maintained
database destination is `text.subtitle_sentence_units` in the unified talent
DuckDB. The sequential full-corpus runner now provides selection, bounded
retry, immediate block checkpoints, and checksum-aware resume behavior.

Current implementation status:

| Component | Current status |
|---|---|
| Raw subtitle ingestion | Operational: `text.subtitle_units` |
| Deterministic overlap removal | Implemented and tested |
| Speaker-turn marker preservation | Implemented and tested |
| Punctuation block construction | Implemented and tested |
| FullStop HTTP client | Implemented and live-tested by the worked example |
| Sentence splitting and approximate timestamps | Implemented and tested |
| Parquet output | Prototype only |
| Derived DuckDB sentence relation | Implemented; created by explicit publication |
| Block checkpoint persistence | Implemented for completed blocks |
| Full-corpus resume orchestration | Implemented; live rollout pending |
| Dashboard use of cleaned sentences | Not yet implemented |

The overview retains one compact worked example so every architectural stage

- [`stream_example.qmd`](stream_example.qmd) processes a real livestream

- [`short_example.qmd`](short_example.qmd) processes a complete real Short

## End-to-end pipeline map

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  A[YouTube subtitle track] --> B[Ingestion pipeline]
  B --> C[text.subtitle_units<br/>canonical raw rows]
  B --> D[ops.source_files and ops.pipeline_runs]
  C --> E[Select pending video and track]
  E --> F[Normalize timestamps and text]
  F --> G[Remove rolling-caption overlap]
  G --> H[Preserve speaker-turn markers]
  H --> I[Build 175-200 word blocks]
  I --> J[FullStop punctuation service<br/>CT 106]
  J --> K[Split punctuated text into sentences]
  K --> L[Allocate approximate sentence timestamps]
  L --> M[Validate completeness and lineage]
  M --> N[text.subtitle_sentence_units<br/>derived DuckDB relation]
  M --> O[ops block checkpoints and pipeline status]
  N --> P[Individual-video dashboard]
```

## Render parameters

From the repository root, resolve the configured DataLake and create the
render-output directory once:

```bash
SUBTITLE_NOTEBOOK_LAKE_ROOT="$(
  Rscript --vanilla -e '
    source("r_scripts/lib/utils/repo_env.R")
    source("r_scripts/lib/utils/datalake_root.r")
    load_repo_env(repo_root = getwd())
    cat(get_datalake_root())
  '
)"
SUBTITLE_NOTEBOOK_OUTPUT_DIR="${SUBTITLE_NOTEBOOK_LAKE_ROOT}/Rendered_Notebooks/transcript_cleaning/pipeline_overview"
mkdir -p "$SUBTITLE_NOTEBOOK_OUTPUT_DIR"
```

Render the database-wide documentation and status checks:

```bash
quarto render r_scripts/notebooks/tests/transcript_cleaning/pipeline_overview.qmd \
  --output-dir "$SUBTITLE_NOTEBOOK_OUTPUT_DIR"
```

Inspect one talent or one video without changing data:

```bash
quarto render r_scripts/notebooks/tests/transcript_cleaning/pipeline_overview.qmd \
  -P talent_code:LEI3 \
  -P video_id:VIDEO_ID \
  --output-dir "$SUBTITLE_NOTEBOOK_OUTPUT_DIR"
```

The optional parameters are:

- `talent_code`: exact talent code from `catalog.talents`.
- `video_id`: exact video identifier. This enables raw-row previews and the
  rolling-caption diagnostic.
- `preview_limit`: maximum raw rows displayed for the selected video.
- `sample_video_id`: live video used by the worked cleaning example. The
  default is an existing Nova Aokami livestream.
- `sample_start_sequence`: first raw caption sequence in the worked example.
- `sample_row_count`: number of consecutive raw captions used in the example.
- `run_punctuation_example`: controls the live FullStop demonstration. The
  default is `true`; deterministic cleaning still runs when it is disabled.
- `publish_example`: explicitly writes the validated sample to DuckDB and reads
  it back. The default is `false`.
- `pipeline_version`: processing version written to sentence and checkpoint
  lineage.

Render without sending the example to FullStop:

```bash
quarto render r_scripts/notebooks/tests/transcript_cleaning/pipeline_overview.qmd \
  -P run_punctuation_example:false \
  --output-dir "$SUBTITLE_NOTEBOOK_OUTPUT_DIR"
```

Run the complete sample pipeline, including the controlled DuckDB write:

```bash
quarto render r_scripts/notebooks/tests/transcript_cleaning/pipeline_overview.qmd \
  -P publish_example:true \
  --output-dir "$SUBTITLE_NOTEBOOK_OUTPUT_DIR"
```

```{r}

required_packages <- c(
  "DBI", "duckdb", "dplyr", "here", "knitr", "purrr", "stringr", "tibble"
)
missing_packages <- required_packages[
  !vapply(required_packages, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)
]
if (length(missing_packages) > 0L) {
  stop(
    "Install the required R packages before rendering: ",
    paste(missing_packages, collapse = ", "),
    call. = FALSE
  )
}

source(here::here("r_scripts", "lib", "utils", "repo_env.R"))
source(here::here("r_scripts", "lib", "utils", "datalake_root.r"))
source(here::here("r_scripts", "lib", "duckdb", "db_connect.R"))
source(here::here(
  "r_scripts", "lib", "clean_data", "clean_subtitles", "clean_subtitles.R"
))
source(here::here(
  "r_scripts", "lib", "clean_data", "clean_subtitles", "punctuation_client.R"
))
source(here::here(
  "r_scripts", "lib", "clean_data", "clean_subtitles", "subtitle_units.R"
))
source(here::here(
  "r_scripts", "lib", "duckdb", "subtitle_sentence_schema.R"
))
source(here::here(
  "r_scripts", "lib", "duckdb", "subtitle_sentence_publish.R"
))

load_repo_env(repo_root = here::here())
db_path <- talent_lakehouse_db_path()
if (!file.exists(db_path)) {
  stop("Unified talent lakehouse not found: ", db_path, call. = FALSE)
}

con <- duckdb_connect(db_path = db_path, read_only = TRUE)

normalize_parameter <- function(value) {
  if (is.null(value) || length(value) == 0L || is.na(value[[1]])) return(NULL)
  value <- trimws(as.character(value[[1]]))
  if (!nzchar(value)) NULL else value
}

talent_code <- normalize_parameter(params$talent_code)
video_id <- normalize_parameter(params$video_id)
preview_limit <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(params$preview_limit))
if (is.na(preview_limit) || preview_limit < 1L) preview_limit <- 25L
sample_video_id <- normalize_parameter(params$sample_video_id)
sample_start_sequence <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(params$sample_start_sequence))
sample_row_count <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(params$sample_row_count))
run_punctuation_example <- isTRUE(params$run_punctuation_example) ||
  tolower(as.character(params$run_punctuation_example)) %in% c("1", "true", "yes")
publish_example <- isTRUE(params$publish_example) ||
  tolower(as.character(params$publish_example)) %in% c("1", "true", "yes")
pipeline_version <- normalize_parameter(params$pipeline_version)
if (is.null(sample_video_id)) {
  stop("sample_video_id must identify one video.", call. = FALSE)
}
if (is.na(sample_start_sequence) || sample_start_sequence < 1L) {
  sample_start_sequence <- 1L
}
if (is.na(sample_row_count) || sample_row_count < 2L) sample_row_count <- 20L
sample_row_count <- min(sample_row_count, 100L)
if (is.null(pipeline_version)) {
  stop("pipeline_version must be one non-empty value.", call. = FALSE)
}
if (publish_example && !run_punctuation_example) {
  stop(
    "publish_example:true requires run_punctuation_example:true.",
    call. = FALSE
  )
}

scope_conditions <- character()
scope_parameters <- list()
if (!is.null(talent_code)) {
  scope_conditions <- c(scope_conditions, "talent_code = ?")
  scope_parameters <- c(scope_parameters, list(talent_code))
}
if (!is.null(video_id)) {
  scope_conditions <- c(scope_conditions, "video_id = ?")
  scope_parameters <- c(scope_parameters, list(video_id))
}
scope_where <- if (length(scope_conditions) == 0L) {
  ""
} else {
  paste("WHERE", paste(scope_conditions, collapse = " AND "))
}

display_table <- function(rows, digits = 2L, caption = NULL) {
  if (nrow(rows) == 0L) {
    rows <- data.frame(message = "No rows matched.")
  }
  knitr::kable(
    rows,
    format = "html",
    digits = digits,
    caption = caption,
    escape = TRUE,
    table.attr = paste(
      'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered table-sm"'
    )
  )
}

relation_exists <- function(schema_name, relation_name) {
  DBI::dbGetQuery(
    con,
    paste(
      "SELECT COUNT(*) = 1 AS available",
      "FROM information_schema.tables",
      "WHERE table_schema = ? AND table_name = ?"
    ),
    params = list(schema_name, relation_name)
  )$available[[1]]
}

configuration <- data.frame(
  item = c(
    "Database", "Talent scope", "Video scope", "Example video",
    "Example calls FullStop", "Example publishes to DuckDB",
    "Pipeline version", "Rendered at"
  ),
  value = c(
    db_path,
    if (is.null(talent_code)) "All talents" else talent_code,
    if (is.null(video_id)) "All videos" else video_id,
    sample_video_id,
    run_punctuation_example,
    publish_example,
    pipeline_version,
    format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", tz = "UTC")
  )
)
display_table(configuration)
```

## Current lakehouse state

The raw table, source-file registry, and pipeline-run registry are upstream
requirements. The derived sentence and checkpoint relations are created by
`init_subtitle_sentence_schema()` during an explicit publication, so they may
be absent in a fresh database until the first approved write.

```{r}
#| label: relation-inventory

relation_inventory <- data.frame(
  role = c(
    "Canonical raw subtitles",
    "Source-file lineage",
    "Pipeline execution history",
    "Derived sentence output",
    "Completed block checkpoints"
  ),
  schema_name = c("text", "ops", "ops", "text", "ops"),
  relation_name = c(
    "subtitle_units",
    "source_files",
    "pipeline_runs",
    "subtitle_sentence_units",
    "subtitle_reconstruction_blocks"
  )
)
relation_inventory$available <- mapply(
  relation_exists,
  relation_inventory$schema_name,
  relation_inventory$relation_name
)
relation_inventory$status <- ifelse(
  relation_inventory$available,
  "AVAILABLE",
  "NOT PRESENT IN DATABASE"
)
display_table(relation_inventory[, c("status", "role", "schema_name", "relation_name")])
```

```{r}
#| label: subtitle-coverage

subtitle_coverage <- DBI::dbGetQuery(
  con,
  paste0(
    "SELECT COUNT(*) AS raw_rows, ",
    "COUNT(DISTINCT video_id) AS videos, ",
    "COUNT(DISTINCT talent_code) AS talents, ",
    "COUNT(DISTINCT subtitle_language) AS recorded_languages ",
    "FROM text.subtitle_units ",
    scope_where
  ),
  params = scope_parameters
)
display_table(subtitle_coverage)
```

```{r}
#| label: raw-schema

raw_schema <- DBI::dbGetQuery(
  con,
  paste(
    "SELECT column_name, data_type, is_nullable",
    "FROM information_schema.columns",
    "WHERE table_schema = 'text' AND table_name = 'subtitle_units'",
    "ORDER BY ordinal_position"

)
display_table(raw_schema)
```

## Stage 1: ingest and preserve raw evidence

Subtitle acquisition belongs to the ingestion repository. Its publisher writes
one keyed row per observed caption into `text.subtitle_units` and registers the
source and execution in `ops.source_files` and `ops.pipeline_runs`.

The cleaning pipeline must never update `subtitle_text` in this raw relation.
Reprocessing must be possible from the original text, timestamps, language,
track type, and source lineage.

The backfill inventory begins from DuckDB—not from the experimental
`Sentence_Units` Parquet folder. It groups raw rows by video and subtitle track,
computes a stable input checksum, and compares that identity with completed
derived work.

## Stage 2: normalize timestamps and text

Raw subtitle timestamps are stored as text such as `00:00:14.150`. The helper
`period_to_seconds()` converts supported timestamp representations into numeric
seconds. Text normalization then:

- converts HTML markers such as `&gt;&gt;` and `&nbsp;`;
- collapses repeated whitespace;
- preserves the original raw row and key for lineage; and
- orders rows by video, track, start time, end time, and sequence number.

The historical `split_timestamp()` helper was designed around CSV-shaped data
and drops columns that the lakehouse needs for lineage. The DuckDB workflow
therefore uses `normalize_subtitle_units_for_reconstruction()`, which retains
`subtitle_unit_key`, `source_file_id`, language, and track type while reusing
`period_to_seconds()`.

### Worked example from a real livestream

The example below reads consecutive raw captions from the canonical DuckDB. By
default it uses Nova Aokami's livestream *stream ends when Symboli Rudolf
Festival comes home*. The title and talent code are queried rather than copied
into the example.

```{r}
#| label: real-sample-load

sample_metadata <- DBI::dbGetQuery(
  con,
  paste(
    "SELECT video.video_id, video.title, video.content_type,",
    "subtitle.talent_code, COUNT(*) AS available_subtitle_rows",
    "FROM catalog.videos AS video",
    "JOIN text.subtitle_units AS subtitle USING (video_id)",
    "WHERE video.video_id = ?",
    "GROUP BY video.video_id, video.title, video.content_type, subtitle.talent_code"
  ),
  params = list(sample_video_id)
)
if (nrow(sample_metadata) != 1L) {
  stop("The sample video did not resolve to exactly one catalog record.", call. = FALSE)
}
display_table(sample_metadata)

sample_raw <- load_subtitle_units_for_reconstruction(
  con,
  video_id = sample_video_id,
  start_sequence = sample_start_sequence,
  row_limit = sample_row_count
)
if (nrow(sample_raw) < 2L) {
  stop("The requested real subtitle sample contains fewer than two rows.", call. = FALSE)
}

sample_prepared <- normalize_subtitle_units_for_reconstruction(sample_raw)

display_table(sample_prepared[, c(
  "sequence_number", "subtitle_start", "subtitle_end", "subtitle_text"
)])
```

```{r}
#| label: raw-preview

if (is.null(video_id)) {

} else {
  raw_preview <- DBI::dbGetQuery(
    con,
    paste0(
      "SELECT subtitle_unit_key, sequence_number, subtitle_start, subtitle_end, ",
      "subtitle_language, subtitle_track_type, subtitle_text ",
      "FROM text.subtitle_units ",
      scope_where,
      " ORDER BY sequence_number LIMIT ",
      preview_limit
    ),
    params = scope_parameters
  )

}
```

## Stage 3: remove rolling-caption repetition

YouTube captions commonly grow over several consecutive rows. Treating every
row as new dialogue repeats most of the transcript.

There are two related deterministic implementations. All maintained project
functions use `snake_case` names:

1. `clean_duplicate_timestamps()` removes a caption when the following longer
   caption contains it, then trims overlap between retained rows.
2. `deduplicate_caption_overlaps()` keeps an accepted word stream and appends
   only the non-overlapping suffix of each new caption.

The second implementation is used by `build_punctuation_blocks()` and is the
foundation for the DuckDB pipeline. Each block and reconstructed sentence now
retains the raw `subtitle_unit_key` values that contributed to it.

```{r}
#| label: real-sample-deduplication

sample_cleaned <- sample_prepared |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    newly_accepted_text = deduplicate_caption_overlaps(.data$text),
    kept = nzchar(.data$newly_accepted_text)
  )

display_table(sample_cleaned[, c(
  "sequence_number", "text", "newly_accepted_text", "kept"
)])

cleaned_transcript <- sample_cleaned |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$kept) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    cleaned_text = stringr::str_squish(paste(.data$newly_accepted_text, collapse = " "))
  )

cleaning_summary <- data.frame(
  measure = c("Raw caption rows", "Rows adding new text", "Raw words", "Accepted words"),
  value = c(
    nrow(sample_cleaned),
    sum(sample_cleaned$kept),
    sum(subtitle_word_count(sample_cleaned$text)),
    subtitle_word_count(cleaned_transcript$cleaned_text)
  )
)
display_table(cleaning_summary)
display_table(cleaned_transcript)
```

### Optional rolling-caption diagnostic

This diagnostic estimates how many rows in one selected video are contained in
the following longer caption. It does not represent the complete overlap
algorithm, but it makes the dominant repetition pattern visible.

```{r}
#| label: rolling-caption-diagnostic

if (is.null(video_id)) {
  display_table(data.frame(message = "Set video_id to run the rolling-caption diagnostic."))
} else {
  rolling_diagnostic <- DBI::dbGetQuery(
    con,
    paste0(
      "WITH ordered AS (",
      "SELECT subtitle_text, LEAD(subtitle_text) OVER (",
      "PARTITION BY video_id, subtitle_language, subtitle_track_type ",
      "ORDER BY sequence_number",
      ") AS next_text FROM text.subtitle_units ",
      scope_where,
      ") SELECT COUNT(*) AS raw_rows, ",
      "COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE next_text IS NOT NULL ",
      "AND LENGTH(next_text) > LENGTH(subtitle_text) ",
      "AND CONTAINS(next_text, subtitle_text)) AS contained_by_next_row ",
      "FROM ordered"
    ),
    params = scope_parameters
  )
  rolling_diagnostic$estimated_repetitive_share <- with(
    rolling_diagnostic,
    ifelse(raw_rows == 0, NA_real_, contained_by_next_row / raw_rows)
  )
  display_table(rolling_diagnostic, digits = 3L)
}
```

## Stage 4: preserve speaker-turn boundaries

Some subtitle tracks use `>>` to mark a new speaker or turn. The function
`expand_speaker_turn_segments()` separates those spans and assigns a stable
`speaker_turn_id` within the video.

This is boundary preservation, not speaker identification. A marker indicates
that the speaker changed, but it does not establish the person's name. The
derived relation should therefore store `speaker_turn_id` and `speaker_change`
without inventing a speaker label.

## Stage 5: build punctuation blocks

FullStop works on text blocks rather than individual rolling captions. The
current defaults target 175 words and cap blocks at 200 words.

`build_punctuation_blocks()`:

- orders caption spans;
- removes exact word overlap;
- respects speaker-turn boundaries;
- normalizes existing punctuation before inference;
- calculates block start and end times; and
- keeps language information for the English-language gate.

```{r}
#| label: real-sample-block-construction

sample_block_input <- sample_prepared
sample_blocks <- build_punctuation_blocks(
  sample_block_input,
  target_words = 175L,
  max_words = 200L,
  talent_name = sample_metadata$talent_code[[1]]
)
display_table(sample_blocks[, c(
  "block_number", "start_sec", "end_sec", "word_count", "model_input_text"
)])
```

## Stage 6: call the FullStop punctuation service

The analytics container uses `punctuate_text()` to send a JSON body containing
one `text` field to:

```text
http://192.168.1.173:8000/v1/punctuate
```

The configured model is:

```text
oliverguhr/fullstop-punctuation-multilang-large
```

The response contains punctuated text and the model identity. FullStop restores
sentence punctuation and capitalization; it does not repair incorrect words
produced by speech recognition.

By default this notebook sends the real cleaned blocks above to FullStop and
displays the returned sentence units. The example does not write its result.
Set `run_punctuation_example:false` when an offline render is required.

```{r}
#| label: optional-real-fullstop-example
#| results: asis

if (!run_punctuation_example) {
  print(display_table(data.frame(
    message = paste(
      "FullStop example disabled; render with",
      "-P run_punctuation_example:true to execute it."
    )
  )))
} else {
  sample_sentences <- reconstruct_sentence_units(
    sample_blocks,
    timeout_sec = 120,
    allow_unknown_language = TRUE
  )
  extract_words <- function(text) {
    tolower(unlist(
      stringr::str_extract_all(
        paste(text, collapse = " "),
        "[[:alnum:]]+(?:['’][[:alnum:]]+)*"
      ),
      use.names = FALSE
    ))
  }
  normalized_sentence_text <- tolower(stringr::str_squish(sample_sentences$text))
  adjacent_duplicates <- if (length(normalized_sentence_text) < 2L) {
    0L
  } else {
    sum(
      normalized_sentence_text[-1L] ==
        normalized_sentence_text[-length(normalized_sentence_text)]
    )
  }
  quality_checks <- data.frame(
    check = c(
      "At least one reconstructed sentence",
      "Every sentence contains a letter or number",
      "Every sentence has terminal punctuation",
      "No adjacent duplicate sentences",
      "Word sequence preserved through punctuation",
      "Sentence timestamps are chronological",
      "Sentence timestamps stay inside the source sample",
      "Model identity returned"
    ),
    pass = c(
      nrow(sample_sentences) > 0L,
      all(stringr::str_detect(sample_sentences$text, "[[:alnum:]]")),
      all(stringr::str_detect(sample_sentences$text, "[.!?][\"'’”]*$")),
      adjacent_duplicates == 0L,
      identical(
        extract_words(sample_blocks$model_input_text),
        extract_words(sample_sentences$text)
      ),
      all(diff(sample_sentences$start_sec) >= 0) &&
        all(sample_sentences$end_sec >= sample_sentences$start_sec),
      min(sample_sentences$start_sec) >= min(sample_blocks$start_sec) &&
        max(sample_sentences$end_sec) <= max(sample_blocks$end_sec),
      all(!is.na(sample_sentences$punctuation_model)) &&
        all(nzchar(sample_sentences$punctuation_model))
    )
  )
  quality_checks$status <- ifelse(quality_checks$pass, "PASS", "FAIL")
  inference_provenance <- data.frame(
    execution_status = "Generated during this render",
    executed_at_utc = format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", tz = "UTC"),
    source_relation = "text.subtitle_units",
    video_id = sample_video_id,
    raw_caption_rows = nrow(sample_raw),
    cleaned_blocks = nrow(sample_blocks),
    output_sentences = nrow(sample_sentences),
    punctuation_model = paste(unique(sample_sentences$punctuation_model), collapse = ", ")
  )
  print(display_table(
    inference_provenance,
    caption = "Inference execution provenance"
  ))
  print(display_table(sample_sentences[, c(
    "sentence_number", "start_sec", "end_sec", "text",
    "punctuation_model", "timestamps_approximate"
  )], caption = "FullStop sentences returned during this render"))
  print(display_table(
    quality_checks[, c("status", "check")],
    caption = "Checks calculated from the returned sentences"
  ))
  if (any(!quality_checks$pass)) {
    stop("The FullStop example failed one or more quality checks.", call. = FALSE)
  }
}
```

A production call must add:

- bounded timeouts;
- retries with exponential backoff for transient failures;
- a maximum attempt count;
- error recording by video and block;
- configurable, load-tested inference concurrency; and
- no retry for deterministic validation failures.

## Stage 7: reconstruct sentences and timestamps

`split_punctuated_sentences()` splits FullStop output at sentence-final
punctuation. `sentence_units_from_block()` then allocates the block duration
across its sentences in proportion to their word counts.

Those timestamps are estimates rather than word-level alignments. Every row
must retain:

```text
timestamps_approximate = true
timestamp_method = block_word_proportion
```

Sentence numbers are assigned in video order after all blocks are assembled.

## Stage 8: validate before publication

A video is publishable only when all required checks pass:

1. Every eligible source block has one successful punctuation response.
2. Blocks and sentences remain in chronological order.
3. Sentence timestamps stay within their source block boundaries.
4. Every sentence has non-empty text and at least one source subtitle key.
5. Every source key resolves to the same video and subtitle track.
6. The recorded model matches the service response.
7. The source checksum still matches the input used to build the blocks.
8. Sentence keys and sequence numbers are unique.
9. The reduction and output-word totals remain within reviewable bounds.

A failed video remains unavailable to downstream consumers until it passes all
video-level checks. Other videos may continue processing.

## Stage 9: publish to DuckDB

The final relation is `text.subtitle_sentence_units`, not a Parquet file.
`init_subtitle_sentence_schema()` creates the derived relation and its
operations checkpoint relation during an explicit write. Its sentence record
shape is:

```sql
-- Documentation excerpt; creation is owned by init_subtitle_sentence_schema().
CREATE TABLE text.subtitle_sentence_units (
  sentence_unit_key VARCHAR PRIMARY KEY,
  video_id VARCHAR NOT NULL,
  channel_id VARCHAR,
  talent_code VARCHAR,
  subtitle_language VARCHAR,
  subtitle_track_type VARCHAR,
  source_scope VARCHAR NOT NULL,
  source_sequence_start BIGINT,
  source_sequence_end BIGINT,
  block_number BIGINT NOT NULL,
  sentence_number BIGINT NOT NULL,
  speaker_turn_id BIGINT,
  speaker_change BOOLEAN NOT NULL,
  start_sec DOUBLE,
  end_sec DOUBLE,
  sentence_text VARCHAR NOT NULL,
  source_subtitle_unit_keys VARCHAR[] NOT NULL,
  source_alignment_status VARCHAR NOT NULL,
  punctuation_model VARCHAR NOT NULL,
  timestamps_approximate BOOLEAN NOT NULL,
  timestamp_method VARCHAR NOT NULL,
  source_checksum_sha256 VARCHAR NOT NULL,
  block_input_checksum_sha256 VARCHAR NOT NULL,
  pipeline_version VARCHAR NOT NULL,
  pipeline_run_id VARCHAR NOT NULL,
  created_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL
);
```

Publication should use one DuckDB writer and one transaction per completed
video/track. Inference workers may run concurrently, but they must return
results to the coordinator rather than opening competing DuckDB writers.

Within a transaction the publisher should:

1. validate the candidate rows and compute the input checksum recorded on them;
2. validate all candidate sentence rows;
3. replace the derived rows for that exact video/track/source scope;
4. mark its block checkpoints complete; and
5. update the corresponding `ops.pipeline_runs` record.

If any step fails, the transaction rolls back and the previous completed
sentence version remains available.

### Dry run, explicit publication, and read-back

The first call below always prepares and validates the exact rows without
writing. When `publish_example:true`, the notebook then closes its read-only
connection, opens one short-lived writer connection, publishes the sentence
and checkpoint rows transactionally, and reopens DuckDB read-only to verify the
saved result.

The partial example is stored with `source_scope = 'notebook_sample'`. It is
therefore isolated from future `full_track` backfill rows and must never be used
as a complete transcript by the dashboard.

```{r}
#| label: duckdb-publication-demonstration
#| results: asis

if (!run_punctuation_example) {
  print(display_table(data.frame(
    message = "FullStop is disabled, so no sentence rows are available to validate or publish."
  )))
} else {
  publication_preview <- publish_subtitle_reconstruction(
    con,
    raw_units = sample_raw,
    blocks = sample_blocks,
    sentence_units = sample_sentences,
    pipeline_version = pipeline_version,
    source_scope = "notebook_sample",
    dry_run = TRUE
  )
  preview_summary <- data.frame(
    action = "Dry run",
    sentence_rows = nrow(publication_preview$sentence_rows),
    checkpoint_rows = nrow(publication_preview$checkpoint_rows),
    source_checksum_sha256 = publication_preview$source_checksum_sha256,
    database_changed = publication_preview$published
  )
  print(display_table(
    preview_summary,
    caption = "Validated publication preview generated during this render"
  ))

  if (!publish_example) {
    existing_rows <- load_published_subtitle_sentences(
      con,
      video_id = sample_video_id,
      source_scope = "notebook_sample"
    )
    if (nrow(existing_rows) == 0L) {
      print(display_table(data.frame(
        message = paste(
          "Dry run passed. Render with -P publish_example:true to write and",
          "read back this isolated notebook sample."
        )
      )))
    } else {
      print(display_table(existing_rows[, c(
        "sentence_number", "start_sec", "end_sec", "sentence_text",
        "punctuation_model", "pipeline_version", "pipeline_run_id"
      )]))
    }
  } else {
    DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)
    con <- NULL

    write_con <- duckdb_connect(db_path = db_path, read_only = FALSE)
    publication <- tryCatch(
      publish_subtitle_reconstruction(
        write_con,
        raw_units = sample_raw,
        blocks = sample_blocks,
        sentence_units = sample_sentences,
        pipeline_version = pipeline_version,
        source_scope = "notebook_sample",
        dry_run = FALSE
      ),
      finally = DBI::dbDisconnect(write_con, shutdown = TRUE)
    )

    con <- duckdb_connect(db_path = db_path, read_only = TRUE)
    persisted_sentences <- load_published_subtitle_sentences(
      con,
      video_id = sample_video_id,
      source_scope = "notebook_sample"
    )
    persisted_checkpoints <- DBI::dbGetQuery(
      con,
      paste(
        "SELECT block_number, status, attempt_count, punctuation_model,",
        "source_checksum_sha256, pipeline_version, pipeline_run_id, updated_at",
        "FROM ops.subtitle_reconstruction_blocks",
        "WHERE video_id = ? AND source_scope = 'notebook_sample'",
        "ORDER BY block_number"
      ),
      params = list(sample_video_id)
    )
    persisted_run <- DBI::dbGetQuery(
      con,
      paste(
        "SELECT pipeline_run_id, pipeline_name, started_at, completed_at,",
        "status, error_summary FROM ops.pipeline_runs",
        "WHERE pipeline_run_id = ?"
      ),
      params = list(publication$pipeline_run_id)
    )

    expected_rows <- publication$sentence_rows |>
      dplyr::arrange(.data$sentence_number)
    observed_rows <- persisted_sentences |>
      dplyr::arrange(.data$sentence_number)
    readback_checks <- data.frame(
      check = c(
        "Published sentence count matches",
        "Sentence keys match",
        "Sentence text matches",
        "Source checksum matches",
        "Pipeline run completed",
        "Every block checkpoint completed"
      ),
      pass = c(
        nrow(observed_rows) == nrow(expected_rows),
        identical(observed_rows$sentence_unit_key, expected_rows$sentence_unit_key),
        identical(observed_rows$sentence_text, expected_rows$sentence_text),
        identical(
          unique(observed_rows$source_checksum_sha256),
          publication$source_checksum_sha256
        ),
        nrow(persisted_run) == 1L && persisted_run$status[[1]] == "completed",
        nrow(persisted_checkpoints) == nrow(sample_blocks) &&
          all(persisted_checkpoints$status == "complete")
      )
    )
    readback_checks$status <- ifelse(readback_checks$pass, "PASS", "FAIL")

    print(display_table(
      persisted_run,
      caption = "Pipeline run read back from ops.pipeline_runs"
    ))
    print(display_table(
      readback_checks[, c("status", "check")],
      caption = "Database read-back checks calculated during this render"
    ))
    print(display_table(persisted_sentences[, c(
      "sentence_number", "start_sec", "end_sec", "sentence_text",
      "source_scope", "punctuation_model", "pipeline_run_id"
    )], caption = "Sentence rows read back from text.subtitle_sentence_units"))
    print(display_table(
      persisted_checkpoints,
      caption = "Block checkpoints read back from ops.subtitle_reconstruction_blocks"
    ))
    if (any(!readback_checks$pass)) {
      stop("DuckDB read-back verification failed.", call. = FALSE)
    }
  }
}
```

## Stage 10: checkpoint and resume the backfill

File-level resume is not sufficient for long livestreams. The publisher records
the state of each punctuation block in
`ops.subtitle_reconstruction_blocks`. The full-track runner consumes those
checkpoints before making another model request.

Each checkpoint needs at least:

- video and track identity;
- source checksum and pipeline version;
- block number and normalized input checksum;
- status: `pending`, `running`, `complete`, or `failed`;
- attempt count and last error;
- punctuation response and model;
- pipeline run ID; and
- created and updated timestamps.

Normal resume skips completed blocks whose checksums and configuration still
match. `retry-failed` selects only failed blocks. `force` intentionally creates
new work for every block in scope.

The initial inventory must run in dry-run mode and report pending, complete,
stale, failed, and unsupported-language videos before any model calls occur.

## Stage 11: full backfill rollout

The safe rollout order is:

1. One short prerecorded video.
2. One long livestream with speaker-turn markers.
3. An intentional interruption followed by resume.
4. One complete talent.
5. A database-wide dry run and request estimate.
6. The full backfill with bounded concurrency.
7. A reconciliation report comparing raw eligible videos with completed
   sentence outputs and failures.

The full run is not complete merely because the command exits. Completion
requires zero unexplained missing videos and an explicit accounting of skipped
languages, empty tracks, validation failures, and exhausted retries.

## Stage 12: dashboard and incremental ingestion

After the backfill is validated, the individual-video dashboard should read
`text.subtitle_sentence_units` for completed videos. Until a video has a valid
derived result, it may fall back to raw `text.subtitle_units` with a clear
status indicator.

New subtitle ingestion should then enqueue only changed video/track checksums.
This makes reconstruction incremental instead of repeatedly scanning and
punctuating the complete corpus.

## Maintained implementation map

- [`clean_subtitles.R`](../../../lib/clean_data/clean_subtitles/clean_subtitles.R)
  contains historical timestamp parsing and deterministic cleaning.
- [`subtitle_units.R`](../../../lib/clean_data/clean_subtitles/subtitle_units.R)
  contains overlap removal, speaker-turn handling, block construction,
  sentence splitting, and approximate timestamp allocation.
- [`punctuation_client.R`](../../../lib/clean_data/clean_subtitles/punctuation_client.R)
  contains the FullStop HTTP client and response validation.
- [`run_subtitle_pipeline.R`](../../../run/Subtitle_clean/run_subtitle_pipeline.R)
  is the current batch runner and experimental Parquet path.
- [`run_sentence_reconstruction.R`](../../../run/Subtitle_clean/run_sentence_reconstruction.R)
  reconstructs one cleaned CSV into the experimental format.
- [`test_subtitle_sentence_reconstruction.R`](../../../tests/test_subtitle_sentence_reconstruction.R)
  records the current transformation behavior.
- [`subtitle_sentence_schema.R`](../../../lib/duckdb/subtitle_sentence_schema.R)
  creates the derived sentence and block-checkpoint relations.
- [`subtitle_sentence_publish.R`](../../../lib/duckdb/subtitle_sentence_publish.R)
  loads canonical subtitle rows, validates reconstruction, publishes one
  scope transactionally, and reads the result back.
- [`subtitle_backfill_tracks.R`](../../../lib/subtitle_backfill/subtitle_backfill_tracks.R)
  discovers tracks, loads one track, and checks whether its result is current.
- [`subtitle_backfill_checkpoints.R`](../../../lib/subtitle_backfill/subtitle_backfill_checkpoints.R)
  builds, loads, validates, and atomically saves resumable checkpoints.
- [`subtitle_backfill_database.R`](../../../lib/subtitle_backfill/subtitle_backfill_database.R)
  owns short-lived DuckDB writes, lock retries, and pipeline-run records.
- [`subtitle_backfill_inference.R`](../../../lib/subtitle_backfill/subtitle_backfill_inference.R)
  runs or reuses punctuation inference for each block.
- [`subtitle_backfill_reconstruction.R`](../../../lib/subtitle_backfill/subtitle_backfill_reconstruction.R)
  validates and publishes one reconstructed video.
- [`subtitle_backfill_runtime.R`](../../../lib/subtitle_backfill/subtitle_backfill_runtime.R)
  reads runner configuration and waits on the collection marker.
- [`subtitle_backfill_batch.R`](../../../lib/subtitle_backfill/subtitle_backfill_batch.R)
  loads and processes one candidate track for the batch runner.
- [`backfill_subtitle_sentences.R`](../../../run/Subtitle_clean/backfill_subtitle_sentences.R)
  selects canonical tracks, skips current results, and coordinates the
  sequential full-track backfill.
- [`test_subtitle_sentence_publish.R`](../../../tests/test_subtitle_sentence_publish.R)
  verifies dry-run safety, lineage, transaction output, and idempotent
  republishing in a temporary DuckDB.
- [`test_subtitle_sentence_backfill.R`](../../../tests/test_subtitle_sentence_backfill.R)
  verifies immediate block checkpointing and zero-request resume behavior.
- [`db_connect.R`](../../../lib/duckdb/db_connect.R) resolves the canonical talent
  lakehouse through `talent_lakehouse_db_path()`.
- [`bin/linux/subtitles/README.md`](../../../../bin/linux/subtitles/README.md)
  documents the existing runner and environment variables.
